summary:
This letter will contain many typos because I’m writing it early in the morn­ ing. We moved to an new apartment and I lost just about all my addresses (I even got my own new address wrong now and then). We wanted to be com­ pletely moved before Tessa went into labor. Well, we did and she did; we now have a little baby boy named Christopher, and I’ll bet I’ve lost his address, too. So this explains why I have not written—until I saw your letter and address in SFC. A good letter, too. 

It’s been so long, I’m not sure what news I’ve already told you. I sold two novels to Doubleday, FLOW MY TEARS, THE POLICEMAN SAID, which is due to be released next Feb. And they bought my half-finished anti-dope novel, A SCANNER DARKLY. All this helped pay for Christopher, who still scowls at us. I think he expected to be born to a richer family, and certainly one not in Ful­ lerton. I think they promised him Bob and Barbara and Terry and Carol as par­ ents, and behold! Ah well. I wish you could see him. He likes to have the radio on by his cradle all night playing semi-rock vocal stuff like Cat Stevens. Other­ wise he cries. 

See, I am making endless typos. Tessa is still sleeping; it is early. Which reminds me of a typo in our local newspaper: CHICKEN FARTS 39C a pound So forgive me for my bad typing.
